summary: Cracks: Abandoned But Not Forgotten is a handcrafted cardboard educational model created by elementary school students for the Abandoned But Not Forgotten challenge. Combining real NASA photographs with curated mission fact cards, the physical display showcases four iconic Mars spacecraft—Curiosity, Viking 1, Mariner 4, and Sojourner—highlighting their historic discoveries, current operational statuses, and legacy in space exploration.
details:
What It Does:

Cracks: Abandoned But Not Forgotten is a physical cardboard educational model that spotlights four landmark NASA Mars missions: Mariner 4, Viking 1, Sojourner, and Curiosity. Through printed photographs paired with clear informational cards, the display teaches viewers what each spacecraft achieved, how Mars exploration evolved over time, and what happens to robotic hardware after its mission ends.

How It Works & How We Built It:

Our elementary school team (grades 2–4) researched the history and status of each spacecraft and constructed a multi-section display out of recycled cardboard. We selected official NASA images of Mariner 4, Viking 1, Sojourner, and Curiosity, wrote concise fact summaries for each one, and arranged them side by side so visitors can visually explore and compare early flyby probes, landers, and rovers.

Why It Matters:

Inactive spacecraft left on Mars or in orbit are much more than space debris—they are milestones of human curiosity and engineering. By bringing together retired pioneers (Mariner 4, Viking 1, and Sojourner) alongside an active rover (Curiosity), our model honors past missions and inspires young learners to care about space history.

Tools & Resources Used:

- Recycled cardboard, printed photographs, markers, and craft supplies

- Official NASA spacecraft photography and historical mission archives for Mariner 4, Viking 1, Sojourner, and Curiosity

- NASA Mars Exploration Program educational resources
